annotations.description: LinuxBridge installs 'bridge' CNI on cluster nodes, so it can be later used to attach Pods/VMs to Linux bridges

command:
cni_mount_dir=/opt/cni/bin
host_dir=/var/lib/cni/bin
components=("bridge" "tuning")
for component in "${components[@]}"; do
  if find "${cni_mount_dir}/${component}" &>/dev/null && ! test -L "${cni_mount_dir}/${component}"; then
    echo "${component} binary found, creating symbolic link ${cni_mount_dir}/cnv-${component}"
    ln -sf "${host_dir}/${component}" "${cni_mount_dir}/cnv-${component}"
  else
    echo "installing cnv-${component}, and creating symbolic link ${cni_mount_dir}/${component}"

    sourcebinpath="/usr/src/github.com/containernetworking/plugins/bin"
    cp --remove-destination "${sourcebinpath}/${component}" "${cni_mount_dir}/cnv-${component}"

    printf -v component_checksum "%s" "$(<${sourcebinpath}/${component}.checksum)"
    printf "%s %s" "${component_checksum% *}" "${cni_mount_dir}/cnv-${component}" | sha256sum --check

    ln -sf "${host_dir}/cnv-${component}" "${cni_mount_dir}/${component}"
  fi
done
echo 'Entering sleep... (success)'
sleep infinity
containers.name: cni-plugins

spec.description:
# Requirements
Your cluster must be installed on bare metal infrastructure with Red Hat Enterprise Linux CoreOS workers.

# Details
**OpenShift Virtualization** extends Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform, allowing you to host and manage virtualized workloads on the same platform as container-based workloads. From the OpenShift Container Platform web console, you can import a VMware virtual machine from vSphere, create new or clone existing VMs, perform live migrations between nodes, and more. You can use OpenShift Virtualization to manage both Linux and Windows VMs.

The technology behind OpenShift Virtualization is developed in the [KubeVirt](https://kubevirt.io) open source community. The KubeVirt project extends [Kubernetes](https://kubernetes.io) by adding additional virtualization resource types through [Custom Resource Definitions](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/access-kubernetes-api/extend-api-custom-resource-definitions/) (CRDs). Administrators can use Custom Resource Definitions to manage `VirtualMachine` resources alongside all other resources that Kubernetes provides.

annotations.description: Automate the management and monitoring of NVIDIA GPUs.

args:
set -e
echo "$(date): Starting GPU VFIO type1 fix"
# Load vfio_iommu_type1 module (provides legacy VFIO container)
if nsenter -t 1 -m -- /usr/sbin/modprobe vfio_iommu_type1 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "$(date): Loaded vfio_iommu_type1 module"
else
  echo "$(date): vfio_iommu_type1 already loaded or failed"
fi
# Verify
if nsenter -t 1 -m -- grep -q vfio_iommu_type1 /proc/modules; then
  echo "$(date): vfio_iommu_type1 is loaded"
else
  echo "$(date): WARNING: vfio_iommu_type1 not loaded"
fi
# Disable runtime PM for NVIDIA GPUs bound to vfio-pci
for dev in $(nsenter -t 1 -m -- ls /sys/bus/pci/drivers/vfio-pci/ 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^[0-9a-f]{4}:' || true); do
  if nsenter -t 1 -m -- cat /sys/bus/pci/devices/$dev/vendor 2>/dev/null | grep -q 0x10de; then
    echo on > /host/sys/bus/pci/devices/$dev/power/control 2>/dev/null || true
    echo "$(date): Set power/control=on for $dev"
  fi
done
# Keep running to maintain the fix (re-apply every 60s)
while true; do
  sleep 60
  # Re-check module
  if ! nsenter -t 1 -m -- grep -q vfio_iommu_type1 /proc/modules 2>/dev/null; then
    nsenter -t 1 -m -- /usr/sbin/modprobe vfio_iommu_type1 2>/dev/null || true
    echo "$(date): Re-loaded vfio_iommu_type1"
  fi
  # Re-check power
  for dev in $(nsenter -t 1 -m -- ls /sys/bus/pci/drivers/vfio-pci/ 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^[0-9a-f]{4}:' || true); do
    if [ "$(cat /host/sys/bus/pci/devices/$dev/power/runtime_status 2>/dev/null)" = "suspended" ]; then
      echo on > /host/sys/bus/pci/devices/$dev/power/control 2>/dev/null || true
      echo "$(date): Resumed $dev from suspend"
    fi
  done
done
containers.name: vfio-fix
